title: Emotional Regulation & The Window of Tolerance
shortDefinition: The biological ability to monitor, modulate, and navigate emotional experiences without becoming hijacked or numbed out.
dailyExample: Feeling a sudden wave of anger or sorrow during a disagreement, but being able to pause, breathe, and speak with intentionality rather than shouting or dissociating.
psychologyTheory: Dr. Dan Siegel's 'Window of Tolerance' model describes the optimal zone of nervous system arousal. Hyperarousal causes fight-or-flight (panic, anger); Hypoarousal causes shutdown (numbness, freeze).
inTherapy: We utilize somatic techniques (breathwork, grounding) paired with cognitive reframing to help widen your nervous system's capacity to tolerate uncomfortable sensations safely.
practicalTakeaway: Emotions are like ocean waves—they crest, peak, and recede within 90 seconds unless fueled by secondary mental storytelling.
